examples.ko: 이 가방은 외국제라서 값이 좀 비싸요.
examples.en: This bag is foreign-made, so it's a bit expensive.

examples.ko: 외국제 화장품은 요즘 인터넷으로 많이 사요.
examples.en: These days people buy a lot of foreign-made cosmetics online.

examples.ko: 외국제보다 국산이 더 좋을 때도 있어요.
examples.en: Sometimes domestic products are better than foreign-made ones.
My grandmother really likes foreign-made watches.
This refrigerator is domestic, not foreign-made.

examples.ko: 가게에서 외국제만 골라서 파는 줄 알았어요.
examples.en: I thought the shop only picked and sold foreign-made goods.

explain: '외제'라고 줄여서 말하는 일이 많아요. 반대말은 '국산'이고, 농산물이나 식재료에는 보통 '외국산'을 써요. '외국제 가방'처럼 만들어진 물건을 말할 때 자연스러워요.
explain_en: People often shorten it to '외제'. The opposite is '국산' (domestic), and for farm products or ingredients people usually say '외국산'. It sounds natural for manufactured items, as in '외국제 가방'.

examples.ko: 이 산길은 외길이라서 길을 잃을 걱정이 없어요.
examples.en: This mountain trail is a single path, so there's no worry about getting lost.

examples.ko: 좁은 외길에서 차를 만나서 한참 뒤로 갔어요.
examples.en: I met a car on the narrow single-lane road and had to back up a long way.

examples.ko: 그분은 평생 한 분야의 외길을 걸어왔어요.
examples.en: He has walked a single path in one field his whole life.
There is only one road to the village.

examples.ko: 그 도자기 장인은 외길 인생을 살았어요.
examples.en: That pottery master lived a life devoted to one path.
It snowed and the single road froze over.

explain: 갈래가 없는 길이라서 '갈림길'과 반대예요. 길 이야기 말고도 한 분야만 계속 가는 삶을 말할 때 '외길 인생'이라고 해요. 이때는 '걷다'와 자주 어울려요.

phrases.en: He spent 30 years devoted solely to pottery.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 가지 일만 오래 해 온 사람을 칭찬하는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It praises someone who has stuck with one kind of work for a long time.
phrases.en_equiv: to devote oneself to one path

explain_en: It is a road with no branches, so it is the opposite of '갈림길' (fork). Besides roads, people use '외길 인생' for a life spent on one field only. In that sense it goes well with the verb '걷다'.

examples.ko: 그 부부는 외딴곳에 작은 집을 짓고 살아요.
examples.en: That couple built a small house in a secluded place and live there.
It's a remote place, so it's very quiet at night.
I walked all the way to a remote place where phones get no signal.
Even though the restaurant is in a remote spot, it has a lot of customers.
I got lost and spent a night in an isolated place.
Wouldn't it be inconvenient to move to a secluded place?

explain: '외딴섬', '외딴집'처럼 '외딴'은 뒤에 장소를 붙여 써요. 쓸쓸하고 다른 곳과 떨어진 느낌이 있어서 '시골'과는 달라요. 시골은 도시가 아닌 지역이고, 외딴곳은 주변과 떨어진 곳이에요.
explain_en: '외딴' attaches to a place noun, as in '외딴섬' and '외딴집'. It has a lonely, cut-off feeling, so it differs from '시골' (countryside), which just means a non-urban area. '외딴곳' stresses being apart from its surroundings.

examples.ko: 산 아래 외딴집에 할머니 혼자 살고 계세요.
examples.en: An old woman lives alone in an isolated house at the foot of the mountain.
It was dark, so I could barely see the light of the lonely house.
Since it's an isolated house, the delivery driver has a hard time finding it.

examples.ko: 우리는 길가의 외딴집에서 물을 얻어 마셨어요.
examples.en: We got some water to drink at a lone house by the road.
That lonely house is famous as a movie filming location.

examples.ko: 외딴집으로 가는 길이 너무 어두워서 무서웠어요.
examples.en: The road to the isolated house was so dark that I was scared.

explain: 이웃집이 가까이 없는 집이라서 이야기나 영화에서 쓸쓸하거나 으스스한 분위기를 낼 때 나오기도 해요. '독채'는 건물 한 채를 다 쓴다는 뜻이라서 달라요. 비슷한 말로 '외딴 곳에 있는 집'이라고 풀어 말해도 돼요.
explain_en: With no neighbors nearby, it can set a lonely or eerie mood in stories and films. '독채' means having a whole building to yourself, so it is different. You can also say '외딴 곳에 있는 집' to spell it out.

examples.ko: 외래문화를 받아들이면서 우리 생활도 많이 바뀌었어요.
examples.en: As we accepted foreign culture, our daily life changed a lot too.
Young people have little resistance to foreign culture.
Halloween is a foreign culture to us, but it has become familiar now.
It's a street where foreign culture and traditional culture blend together.

examples.ko: 외래문화만 무조건 따라 하는 건 좋지 않다고 생각해요.
examples.en: I think it's not good to blindly copy only foreign culture.

examples.ko: 이 수업에서는 외래문화가 언어에 준 영향을 배워요.
examples.en: In this class we learn about the influence foreign culture had on language.

explain: '전통문화', '토착문화'와 짝으로 생각하면 쉬워요. '외래'는 '외래어', '외래종'처럼 밖에서 들어온 것 앞에 붙어요. 문장에 따라 '전통을 위협한다'는 분위기가 될 수도 있어요.
explain_en: It is easy to think of it as a pair with '전통문화' or '토착문화'. '외래' goes before things that came in from outside, as in '외래어' and '외래종'. Depending on the sentence, it can carry a tone of 'threatening tradition'.

examples.ko: 섬에는 천적이 없어서 외래종이 빠르게 퍼졌어요.
examples.en: The island had no natural predators, so the introduced species spread quickly.

examples.ko: 이 호수에는 외래종 물고기가 점점 늘고 있어요.
examples.en: Introduced fish species are gradually increasing in this lake.

examples.ko: 외래종을 함부로 풀어 주면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not carelessly release non-native species.

examples.ko: 외래종 때문에 토종 식물이 사라지고 있어요.
examples.en: Native plants are disappearing because of introduced species.

examples.ko: 저 꽃은 원래 외래종인데 지금은 어디서나 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: That flower was originally an introduced species, but now you can see it everywhere.
The news covered the problem of non-native turtles.

explain: 반대말은 '토종'이에요. 뉴스나 과학 수업에서 생태계 문제와 같이 나올 때가 많아요. '외래 생물'이라고도 말해요.
explain_en: Its opposite is '토종' (native species). It often appears in news or science class together with ecosystem problems. People also say '외래 생물'.

en: unpaid tab; amount owed on credit

examples.ko: 이번 달 외상값은 다음 주까지 꼭 갚을게요.
examples.en: I'll definitely pay this month's tab by next week.
The shop owner called about the unpaid tab.

examples.ko: 외상값이 쌓여서 이제는 더 못 사요.
examples.en: The tab has piled up, so I can't buy any more now.
My father collected the outstanding bill from a client.
Please settle the whole tab at once at the end of the month.

examples.ko: 친구에게 빌린 돈이 아니라 식당 외상값이에요.
examples.en: It's not money borrowed from a friend, it's a restaurant tab.

explain: '외상'은 물건을 먼저 받고 돈은 나중에 내는 거래예요. 그래서 '외상으로 사다', '외상값을 갚다/받다'처럼 짝지어 써요. 가게에 '외상 사절'이라고 써 붙이기도 해요.
explain_en: '외상' is buying first and paying later, so it pairs as '외상으로 사다' and '외상값을 갚다/받다'. Some shops put up a sign saying '외상 사절' (no credit).

examples.ko: 할머니는 외손자가 오는 날을 손꼽아 기다리세요.
examples.en: Grandmother counts the days until her grandson visits.
Our grandson has already become an elementary school student.

examples.ko: 외손자에게 용돈을 주고 싶어서 은행에 갔어요.
examples.en: I went to the bank because I wanted to give my grandson some pocket money.

examples.ko: 할아버지께서 외손자 이름을 직접 지어 주셨어요.
examples.en: Grandfather named his grandson himself.
He is a person who cherishes his daughter's son and his son's son equally.

examples.ko: 마을 어른들께 외할아버지 성함을 말하며 외손자라고 인사드렸어요.
examples.en: I greeted the village elders by saying my maternal grandfather's name and that I was his grandson.

explain: 아들 쪽 손자는 '친손자'라고 구별해요. 손녀는 '외손녀'예요. 앞에서 부를 때는 보통 이름으로 부르고, '외손자'는 남에게 소개하거나 이야기할 때 써요.
explain_en: A grandson on the son's side is called '친손자', to tell them apart. A granddaughter is '외손녀'. To their face people usually call them by name; '외손자' is used when introducing or talking about them.

examples.en: This store sells only foreign-made products.

examples.ko: 외제품이라고 해서 다 품질이 좋은 건 아니에요.
examples.en: Just because something is foreign-made doesn't mean its quality is always good.

examples.ko: 요즘은 외제품을 해외 직구로 많이 사요.
examples.en: These days people buy a lot of foreign products through overseas direct purchase.

examples.ko: 부모님은 외제품보다 국산 제품을 더 믿으세요.
examples.en: My parents trust domestic products more than foreign ones.
There are so many foreign products in the airport duty-free shop.
There was a campaign to reduce the use of foreign products.

explain: '외국제', '외제'와 거의 같은 말이에요. 반대말은 '국산품'이에요. 가방, 가전, 화장품처럼 파는 물건 이야기에서 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It is almost the same as '외국제' and '외제'. The opposite is '국산품' (domestic goods). It sounds natural when talking about goods for sale, like bags, appliances and cosmetics.

examples.ko: 광대가 외줄 위에서 춤을 추듯 걸어요.
examples.en: The performer walks on a single rope as if dancing.

examples.ko: 외줄을 타는 모습을 보니 손에 땀이 났어요.
examples.en: Watching him walk the tightrope made my palms sweat.
This necklace is a single strand, so it's simple and neat.

examples.ko: 외줄로 서지 말고 두 줄로 서 주세요.
examples.en: Please don't stand in a single line, stand in two lines.
The bridge was as thin as a single rope, so it was scary to cross.

examples.ko: 외줄 타기는 균형 감각이 아주 중요해요.
examples.en: Tightrope walking requires a very good sense of balance.

explain: 줄이 한 가닥뿐일 때 써요. 반대는 '두 줄'처럼 줄이 여러 개일 때예요. '외줄 타기'는 줄 하나 위를 걷는 공연이에요.

phrases.example: 요즘 회사 사정이 외줄 타기 같아요.
phrases.en: These days the company's situation feels like walking a tightrope.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조금만 실수해도 무너질 것 같은 아슬아슬한 상황을 비유해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It describes a precarious situation where one small mistake could cause a collapse.

explain_en: It is used when there is only one strand or line. The opposite is several lines, such as '두 줄'. '외줄 타기' is the performance of walking on a single rope.

examples.ko: 이 마을은 외지인에게 조금 불친절하다고 해요.
examples.en: They say this village is a bit unfriendly to outsiders.
In the tourist season, many outsiders come to visit.
Judging from the way he talked, he seemed like an outsider.
I'm not from around here, so I don't know the roads well.
Outsiders bought land, so housing prices went up.

examples.ko: 이곳에서 오래 살았는데도 아직 외지인으로 보는 사람이 있어요.
examples.en: Even though I've lived here a long time, some people still see me as an outsider.

explain: 그 지역에서 나고 자란 '토박이'나 '현지인'과 반대로 말해요. 다른 지역에서 온 사람이라는 느낌이 강해서, 말투에 따라 거리를 두는 느낌이 날 수 있어요. 직접 말할 때는 '다른 지역에서 오신 분'이라고 하면 부드러워요.
explain_en: It is the opposite of '토박이' (native) or '현지인' (local). It strongly means someone from another region, so depending on tone it can feel distant. When speaking directly to someone, '다른 지역에서 오신 분' sounds softer.

examples.ko: 고속도로 요금소 앞에서 차가 많이 막혀요.
examples.en: Traffic is heavily jammed in front of the highway tollgate.
We passed through the tollgate in the Hi-Pass lane.

examples.ko: 다음 요금소까지 얼마나 더 가야 해요?
examples.en: How much farther is it to the next tollgate?
The tollgate staff told me the toll.
A rest stop appears right after the tollgate.
You can also pay by card at the tollgate.

explain: '톨게이트'라고 말하는 사람도 많아요. 요즘은 '하이패스' 차로로 멈추지 않고 지나가는 일도 있어요. '요금소를 지나다/통과하다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: Many people also say '톨게이트'. These days you can pass through a '하이패스' lane without stopping. It is used like '요금소를 지나다/통과하다'.

examples.en: Next time, I'll buy the coffee.
You can get off at the very next stop.
I'm busy today, so let's meet next time.
Who is next in the presentation order?

examples.ko: 이번엔 졌지만 요다음엔 꼭 이길 거예요.
examples.en: I lost this time, but I'll definitely win next time.
Please transfer at the next station.

explain: '다음'보다 가깝고 친근한 느낌이에요. 말할 때 '요다음에 보자'처럼 쓰고, 윗사람이나 격식 있는 자리에서는 '다음에'가 더 안전해요. '요번', '요전'처럼 '요-'가 붙는 말들과 한 무리예요.
explain_en: It feels closer and friendlier than '다음'. People say it in talk like '요다음에 보자', but with elders or in formal settings plain '다음에' is safer. It belongs to the group of '요-' words like '요번' and '요전'.

en: be shaken; be rocked; be jolted

examples.ko: 배가 파도에 크게 요동쳐서 멀미가 났어요.
examples.en: The boat rocked heavily on the waves and I got seasick.

examples.ko: 시험 결과를 기다리는 동안 마음이 요동쳤어요.
examples.en: My heart was in turmoil while waiting for the exam results.
The exchange rate has been fluctuating wildly lately, and I'm worried.
You have to stay calm when stock prices swing wildly.
The road is bumpy, so the car keeps jolting.

examples.ko: 그 말을 듣자 심장이 요동치기 시작했어요.
examples.en: As soon as I heard that, my heart started pounding.

explain: 배, 차, 땅처럼 크게 흔들릴 때 쓰고, 마음·가격·분위기가 크게 출렁일 때도 써요. '흔들리다'보다 움직임이 크고 거칠어요. '요동쳐요/요동쳤어요'로 활용해요.
explain_en: It is used when things like boats, cars and the ground shake hard, and also when feelings, prices or moods swing sharply. The movement is bigger and rougher than with '흔들리다'. It conjugates as '요동쳐요/요동쳤어요'.

en: this way and that; from every angle

examples.en: The child plays, turning the toy this way and that.
The cat dodged my hand this way and that.
I looked over the clothes from every angle in front of the mirror.
The road was jammed, so I wove through the alleys.

examples.ko: 문제를 요리조리 생각해 봐도 답을 모르겠어요.
examples.en: I've thought about the problem every which way, but I don't know the answer.
The fish slipped out of the net, darting this way and that.

explain: '아무렇게나'가 아니라 이쪽저쪽 방향을 바꾸며 움직이거나 살필 때 써요. 조금 귀엽고 가벼운 말투예요. 아이나 동물의 움직임에 특히 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It does not mean 'carelessly'; it means moving or looking this way and that, changing direction. It has a slightly cute, light tone. It suits the movements of children and animals especially well.

en: this bit; this little; this much

examples.ko: 배가 불러서 밥은 요만큼만 주셔도 돼요.
examples.en: I'm full, so you can give me just this much rice.

examples.ko: 동생이 요만큼 작았을 때 처음 만났어요.
examples.en: I first met my younger sibling when they were this small.

examples.ko: 저는 그런 일이 있었다는 걸 요만큼도 몰랐어요.
examples.en: I had no idea at all that something like that had happened.

examples.ko: 내가 한 말에 요만큼의 거짓도 없어요.
examples.en: There isn't a bit of a lie in what I said.

examples.ko: 케이크를 요만큼 남겨 뒀으니까 먹어 봐요.
examples.en: I left this much cake, so try some.
The child showed me with their fingers that it was about this much.

explain: '이만큼'보다 작고 가까운 양이나 크기를 말해요. 손가락으로 크기를 보여 주면서 말할 때가 많아요. '요만큼도 없다'처럼 부정문과 같이 쓰면 '전혀'라는 강한 느낌이 돼요.
explain_en: It points to a smaller, closer amount or size than '이만큼'. People often say it while showing the size with their fingers. With a negative, as in '요만큼도 없다', it strongly means 'not at all'.

en: to be strange; to be odd

examples.en: This food smells a bit odd.
I heard a strange sound and looked behind me.
Since yesterday the machine has been acting weird.
That person's outfit looked strange.
I thought it looked odd, but it tasted good when I tried it.

examples.ko: 꿈이 너무 요상해서 친구한테 얘기해 줬어요.
examples.en: My dream was so weird that I told my friend about it.

explain: '이상하다'보다 입말 느낌이 강하고, 조금 장난스럽거나 못마땅한 느낌이 들어요. 글이나 발표보다 편한 대화에서 어울려요. '요상한 + 명사', '요상하게 + 동사'로 많이 써요.
explain_en: It feels more colloquial than '이상하다' and can sound a bit playful or disapproving. It fits casual conversation better than writing or presentations. It is often used as '요상한 + noun' or '요상하게 + verb'.

examples.en: My uncle has worked in the restaurant business for over ten years.

examples.ko: 요식업은 사람을 대하는 일이 많아서 힘들어요.
examples.en: The food service industry is tough because you deal with a lot of people.

examples.ko: 요즘 요식업 창업이 어려워졌다는 뉴스를 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw news that starting a restaurant business has gotten harder lately.

examples.ko: 요식업을 하려면 위생 관리가 정말 중요해요.
examples.en: If you want to run a restaurant business, hygiene management is really important.

examples.ko: 코로나 이후로 요식업 매출이 크게 줄었어요.
examples.en: Since COVID, sales in the food service industry have dropped sharply.
I want to work in the food service field.

explain: 일상에서는 '식당을 하다'라고 말하고, '요식업'은 창업이나 경제 뉴스에서 보여요. '외식업'이라고도 해요. 식당, 카페처럼 음식을 파는 일 전체를 넓게 가리켜요.
explain_en: In daily talk people say '식당을 하다', while '요식업' shows up in startup and economic news. It is also called '외식업'. It broadly covers all work of selling food, like restaurants and cafes.

examples.en: I bought the book you mentioned the other day.
The other time, it rained so I couldn't go.
Why didn't you come to the last gathering?
I made the very same mistake as last time again.
Thank you so much for helping me the other day.
What was the name of the restaurant we went to the other day?

explain: '지난번'과 비슷한데 더 가볍게 말할 때 써요. '요전'만 쓰기도 해요. 윗사람에게 격식 있게 말할 때는 '지난번'이 무난해요.
explain_en: It is close to '지난번' but used in a lighter tone. People sometimes say just '요전'. When speaking formally to elders, '지난번' is the safe choice.

examples.ko: 필요한 자료를 요청서에 적어서 보내 주세요.
examples.en: Please write the materials you need on the request form and send it.
A week has passed since I submitted the request.
This request form needs the team leader's approval.

examples.ko: 요청서 맨 위에 이름과 연락처를 꼭 쓰세요.
examples.en: Be sure to write your name and contact number at the top of the request form.
The repair request hasn't been processed yet.

examples.ko: 담당자가 요청서를 읽고 바로 답장을 줬어요.
examples.en: The person in charge read the request and replied right away.

explain: '신청서'는 정식으로 신청할 때, '요청서'는 무언가를 해 달라고 부탁하는 문서일 때 써요. '요청서를 제출하다/작성하다/보내다'처럼 써요. 앞에 '수리', '자료'처럼 내용을 붙여 말해요.
explain_en: '신청서' is for a formal application, while '요청서' is a document asking for something to be done. It is used as '요청서를 제출하다/작성하다/보내다'. People put the content in front, like '수리' or '자료'.

examples.en: If I sit for a long time, I get a backache.
I get physical therapy at the hospital because of back pain.

examples.ko: 아버지는 요통으로 오래 서 있기 힘드세요.
examples.en: My father finds it hard to stand for long because of lower back pain.

examples.ko: 요통에는 가벼운 걷기 운동이 도움이 돼요.
examples.en: Light walking exercise helps with lower back pain.

examples.ko: 요통은 한 번 생기면 오래가기도 해요.
examples.en: Once you get lower back pain, it can sometimes last a long time.
If the back pain continues, get it checked.

explain: 일상에서는 '허리가 아프다', '허리 통증'이라고 많이 말해요. '요통'은 병원이나 건강 정보에서 더 자주 보여요. '허리'는 몸의 부위이고 '요통'은 아픈 증상을 가리켜요.
explain_en: In daily life people more often say '허리가 아프다' or '허리 통증'. '요통' appears more in hospitals and health information. '허리' is the body part, while '요통' refers to the pain symptom.

examples.en: The grandmother at that restaurant is famous for her salty tongue.

examples.ko: 욕쟁이 할머니의 국밥집에 사람들이 줄을 서요.
examples.en: People line up at the soup restaurant of the foul-mouthed grandmother.
That friend swears a lot, but has a warm heart.

examples.ko: 욕쟁이처럼 말하지 말고 예쁘게 말해 보세요.
examples.en: Don't talk like a potty mouth, try speaking nicely.
I heard my uncle was foul-mouthed in the old days.
I was upset to be told I sounded like a potty mouth.

explain: '욕쟁이 할머니' 맛집처럼 겉은 거칠어도 정이 있는 사람에게 쓰기도 해요. 하지만 다른 사람에게 직접 쓰면 기분 나빠할 수 있어요. '-쟁이'가 붙어 어떤 버릇이 있는 사람을 가리켜요.
explain_en: It is sometimes used for someone rough on the outside but warm inside, as in the '욕쟁이 할머니' restaurants. Still, saying it directly to someone can offend them. The '-쟁이' ending marks a person with a certain habit.

examples.en: He bravely jumped into the flames.
I bravely raised my hand and asked a question.
Even though the child was scared, he bravely took the shot.
We applauded the players who fought bravely.

examples.ko: 잘못을 용감히 인정하는 것도 쉽지 않아요.
examples.en: It's not easy to courageously admit your mistakes either.

examples.ko: 그녀는 용감히 앞으로 나서서 도와 달라고 외쳤어요.
examples.en: She bravely stepped forward and shouted for help.

explain: '용감하게'가 더 일상적인 말이고, '용감히'는 이야기나 글에서 더 어울려요. 뒤에 오는 동사를 꾸며 줘요. 반대 느낌의 말로는 '겁먹은 채로', '주저하며'가 있어요.
explain_en: '용감하게' is the more everyday form, while '용감히' suits stories and writing more. It modifies the verb that follows. For the opposite feeling, you can use '겁먹은 채로' or '주저하며'.

examples.en: In Byeoljubujeon, the turtle takes the rabbit to the Dragon Palace.
I read the story of the rabbit who went to the Dragon Palace.
They say the Dragon King lives in the undersea Dragon Palace.
In that cartoon, the Dragon Palace appears in a splendid way.
The children imagined the Dragon Palace and drew a picture.
I visited an aquarium as splendid as a Dragon Palace.

explain: 옛이야기 속 바닷속 세계라서 상상 속 장소로만 말해요. '수궁'이라고도 해요. 가게나 시설 이름에 쓰이기도 해요.
explain_en: It is a world under the sea from old tales, so it is spoken of only as an imaginary place. It is also called '수궁'. It is sometimes used in the names of shops and facilities.

examples.ko: 이사할 때 용달차를 불러서 짐을 옮겼어요.
examples.en: When I moved, I called a delivery truck to carry the things.

examples.ko: 용달차 기사님이 짐을 같이 날라 주셨어요.
examples.en: The delivery truck driver helped carry the luggage with me.

examples.ko: 작은 가구는 용달차 한 대면 충분해요.
examples.en: For small furniture, one delivery truck is enough.
I sent the flower pots to the country house by delivery truck.
A delivery truck is parked at the front of the alley.
The delivery truck fee varies by distance.

explain: 작은 트럭으로 이삿짐이나 물건을 날라 주는 차에 써요. '용달차를 부르다'처럼 필요할 때 불러서 쓰는 느낌이에요. 큰 이사에는 '이삿짐센터'를 부르기도 해요.
explain_en: It is used for a small truck that carries moving goods and other items. It feels like something you call when needed, as in '용달차를 부르다'. For big moves, people may call a '이삿짐센터' (moving company) instead.

examples.en: There is a spring inside the ballpoint pen.
The bed spring is broken and makes a noise.
I sprang up like a spring and caught the ball.
The child rolled a spring toy down the stairs.
If you press the spring hard, it pops back out.
The springs inside the mattress are old and have stretched.

explain: '스프링'이라고도 말해요. 볼펜, 침대, 장난감처럼 눌렀다 놓으면 되돌아오는 부품에 써요. '용수철 장난감'처럼 다른 명사 앞에 붙여 쓰기도 해요.
explain_en: People also say '스프링'. It is used for parts that return to shape after being pressed, like in pens, beds and toys. It can also go before another noun, as in '용수철 장난감'.

examples.ko: 컵이 우그러져 있어서 새 걸 샀어요.
examples.en: The cup was dented, so I bought a new one.
The pot got dented and is inconvenient to use.
The car door got hit and ended up dented.
When I stepped on the can, it got crushed easily.
I tried straightening the crumpled hat with my hands.
Carry the box carefully so it doesn't get dented.

explain: 눌리거나 부딪혀서 한쪽이 안으로 들어가고 모양이 망가질 때 써요. 비슷한 말로 '찌그러지다'를 쓰는 사람도 많아요. 캔, 냄비, 자동차처럼 단단한 물건에 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It is used when something is pressed or hit so one side caves in and the shape is spoiled. Many people also say the similar '찌그러지다'. It suits hard objects such as cans, pots and cars.

examples.en: My younger sibling received an honor award at the end of the term.

examples.ko: 우등상 받은 날 부모님이 맛있는 걸 사 주셨어요.
examples.en: On the day I got the honor prize, my parents bought me something tasty.

examples.ko: 우등상은 성적이 아주 좋은 학생에게 줘요.
examples.en: The honor prize is given to students with very good grades.
I received an honor award certificate at the graduation ceremony.

examples.ko: 우등상보다 개근상이 더 어렵다고 하는 사람도 있어요.
examples.en: Some people say perfect attendance is harder to get than an honor prize.
Since the honor prize was my goal, I studied hard.

explain: 성적이 좋은 학생에게 주는 상이라서 학교 이야기에서 나와요. 학교에 빠짐없이 나온 학생에게는 '개근상'을 줘요. '우등생'은 성적이 좋은 학생이고, '우등상'은 그 상이에요.
explain_en: It is a prize for students with good grades, so it comes up in school talk. A student who never missed school gets a '개근상' (perfect attendance award). '우등생' is the high-achieving student, and '우등상' is the prize.

en: look up to; look up at

examples.en: I have looked up to my older brother since childhood.
People admired that teacher and followed him.
I lifted my head and looked up at the stars in the sky.
He is an actor everyone looks up to.
If you only look up to someone, your confidence shrinks.
I look up to and respect my parents.

explain: 고개를 들어 위를 보는 뜻도 있고, 훌륭하다고 존경하는 뜻으로도 써요. 반대는 '내려다보다'이고, 낮게 보는 뜻으로는 '깔보다'를 써요. 사람에게 쓸 때는 '~를 우러러보다'로 말해요.
explain_en: It can mean lifting your head to look up, and also to look up to someone with respect. The opposite is '내려다보다', and for looking down on someone you use '깔보다'. For people it is said as '~를 우러러보다'.

examples.en: I make a broth from anchovies and boil the soup.
I boiled the beef bones for a long time and drew out the broth.
Steep the tea leaves in warm water and drink it.

examples.ko: 우려내는 시간이 길면 맛이 쓸 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you steep it too long, it can taste bitter.
Cool the steeped water and keep it in the refrigerator.

examples.ko: 뼈에서 진한 맛을 우려내려면 시간이 필요해요.
examples.en: To draw a rich flavor out of the bones, you need time.

explain: 재료를 물에 담가 끓이거나 담가 두어서 맛과 성분이 나오게 할 때 써요. 육수, 차, 약재에 자주 어울려요. 남에게서 돈이나 물건을 꾀로 빼내는 뜻으로도 쓰이니 문장을 보고 구별하세요.
explain_en: It is used when you soak or boil an ingredient in water so its flavor and substance come out. It goes well with broth, tea and herbal medicine. It can also mean getting money or things out of someone by tricks, so tell them apart by context.

examples.ko: 사골 뼈를 한 번 더 우려먹었어요.
examples.en: I boiled the beef bones one more time for another broth.

examples.ko: 그 감독은 같은 소재만 계속 우려먹는다는 말을 들어요.
examples.en: That director gets told he keeps rehashing the same material.
Don't milk the same joke again.

examples.ko: 한 번 쓴 티백을 다시 우려먹으면 맛이 약해요.
examples.en: If you reuse a used tea bag, the taste is weak.
My senior keeps rehashing his old success story, and I'm sick of it.

examples.ko: 제작사는 그 인기를 더 우려먹으려고 해요.
examples.en: The production company wants to milk that popularity even more.

explain: 한 번 쓴 재료를 다시 끓이거나 담가 쓸 때 써요. 요즘은 같은 이야기나 성공을 계속 써먹는 뜻으로 더 많이 쓰고, 조금 못마땅한 느낌이 있어요. '재탕하다'와 가까운 말이에요.
explain_en: It is used when you boil or steep an already-used ingredient again. It is now used more for reusing the same story or success again and again, with a slightly disapproving tone. It is close to '재탕하다'.

en: our script (Hangeul); the Korean writing system

examples.en: Hangeul is our own script, so I'm really proud of it.
I practice writing in our script every day.

examples.ko: 외국에서 오래 살다 보니 우리글이 그리워요.
examples.en: After living abroad for a long time, I miss our own script.
King Sejong created our script for the people.
I translated a poem written in Korean into a foreign language.
It's important to cherish our written and spoken language.

explain: 주로 '한글'을 가리키지만 '우리'가 들어가서 자부심이나 애정이 느껴져요. '우리말'은 말, '우리글'은 글이라서 짝으로 많이 말해요. 외국 사람이 한국 글을 말할 때는 보통 '한글'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It mainly points to Hangeul, but the word '우리' adds a feeling of pride and affection. '우리말' is the spoken language and '우리글' the written one, so they are often paired. A foreigner talking about the Korean script would usually just say '한글'.

examples.en: In the old days, villagers gathered around the well.
My grandmother did the laundry by the well.
There was a big persimmon tree next to the well.
The area around a well is a dangerous place for children.

examples.ko: 영화 속 우물가 장면이 인상 깊었어요.
examples.en: The scene by the well in the movie was impressive.
I went to the well to fetch water.

explain: 우물 둘레를 말하는데, 옛 마을의 모습을 떠올리게 하는 말이에요. 요즘 생활보다는 옛이야기나 드라마에서 많이 들려요. '물가', '강가'처럼 '-가'가 붙어서 그 곁이라는 느낌을 줘요.
explain_en: It means the area around a well, and it brings to mind scenes of old villages. You hear it more in old tales and dramas than in modern life. Like '물가' and '강가', the '-가' adds the sense of 'beside' something.

examples.en: I dithered and missed the last bus.
He hesitated and couldn't answer.

examples.ko: 할 말이 있으면 우물쭈물하지 말고 말해 보세요.
examples.en: If you have something to say, don't hesitate, just say it.
I hesitated in the interview, and I felt really sorry about it.

examples.ko: 아이가 문 앞에서 우물쭈물 서 있었어요.
examples.en: The child was standing at the door, hesitating.
While I was hesitating, the seats ran out.

explain: 자신이 없어서 말이나 행동을 확실히 못 하고 머뭇거릴 때 써요. 비슷한 말로 '머뭇거리다', '주저하다'가 있는데, 우물쭈물은 조금 답답하고 소심해 보이는 느낌이에요. '우물쭈물하다'로도 많이 쓰고, 부정적인 말투일 때가 많아요.
explain_en: It is used when someone hesitates in speech or action because they lack confidence. Similar words are '머뭇거리다' and '주저하다', but '우물쭈물' feels a bit frustrating and timid. It is also often used as '우물쭈물하다', and usually has a negative tone.
